subQuestions.questionText:
Refer to TABLE 1 (Sarah's till slip from a supermarket — all prices include VAT at 15%). The table includes: Brown bread (qty 2, unit price R18,00, total = A); Milk 2L (qty 1, R32,99, R32,99); Apples (qty 5, R6,50, R32,50); Sugar 2,5kg (qty 1, R64,95, R64,95); Cooking oil 750mL (qty 1, R89,99, R89,99); Eggs 1 dozen (qty 1, R49,50, R49,50); SUB-TOTAL incl. VAT = B.

Calculate the value of A on the till slip.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Method: $A = \text{quantity} \times \text{unit price} = 2 \times R18,00$ ✓
Mark 2: Answer: $A = R36,00$ ✓
Total: 2 marks

subQuestions.questionText: (Refer to TABLE 1 in the question paper.) Calculate the value of B, the sub-total of the bill (including VAT).
(Refer to TABLE 1 in the question paper.) Calculate the amount of VAT included in the sub-total B. Round your answer to TWO decimal places.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Formula: $\text{VAT included} = B \times \frac{15}{115}$ ✓
Mark 2: Substitution: $\text{VAT} = 305,93 \times \frac{15}{115} = \frac{4\,588,95}{115}$ ✓
Mark 3: Answer: $\text{VAT} = R39,90$ ✓
Total: 3 marks

subQuestions.questionText: Sarah pays the cashier with two R200 notes. Calculate her change.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Method: $\text{Change} = (2 \times R200) - R305,93 = R400 - R305,93$ ✓
Mark 2: Answer: $\text{Change} = R94,07$ ✓
Total: 2 marks

subQuestions.questionText: Write the cost of the brown bread (value A) to the cost of the eggs as a ratio in simplest form.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Set up ratio: $\text{Bread} : \text{Eggs} = R36,00 : R49,50$ ✓
Mark 2: Multiply both by 2 to remove decimals: $72 : 99$ ✓
Mark 3: Divide both by 9 (HCF): $\text{Ratio} = 8 : 11$ ✓
Total: 3 marks

subQuestions.questionText:
INFORMATION 2: There are 30 learners in Sarah's Grade 12 class. The class consists of 18 girls and 12 boys. The teacher chooses ONE learner at random to answer a question.

Write the number of boys to the total number of learners as a ratio in simplest form.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Set up ratio: $\text{Boys} : \text{Total} = 12 : 30$ ✓
Mark 2: Divide both by 6 (HCF): $\text{Ratio} = 2 : 5$ ✓
Total: 2 marks

subQuestions.questionText: Determine the probability (as a decimal, rounded to TWO decimal places) that a girl is chosen.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Method: $P(\text{girl}) = \frac{\text{number of girls}}{\text{total}} = \frac{18}{30}$ ✓
Mark 2: Answer: $P(\text{girl}) = 0,60$ ✓
Total: 2 marks

subQuestions.questionText: Write your answer to QUESTION 1.2.2 as a percentage.

INFORMATION 3 — Sipho's Monthly Cellphone Costs (TABLE 2):
Voice calls: 240 minutes per month at R1,20 per minute
SMS messages: 80 messages per month at R0,50 per message
Mobile data: 2 GB per month at R49,00 per GB

Calculate Sipho's TOTAL monthly cellphone cost.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Calls: $240 \times R1,20 = R288,00$ ✓
Mark 2: SMS: $80 \times R0,50 = R40,00$ ✓
Mark 3: Data: $2 \times R49,00 = R98,00$ ✓
Mark 4: Total: $R288,00 + R40,00 + R98,00 = R426,00$ ✓
Total: 4 marks

subQuestions.questionText: The next month, the service provider increased ALL rates by 8%. Calculate the new total monthly cost. Round to TWO decimal places.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Method: $\text{New total} = \text{old total} \times 1,08$ ✓
Mark 2: Substitution: $R426,00 \times 1,08$ ✓
Mark 3: Answer: $\text{New total} = R460,08$ ✓
Total: 3 marks

subQuestions.questionText: Express the cost of voice calls as a percentage of the original total cost calculated in QUESTION 1.3.1. Round to TWO decimal places.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Formula: $\% = \frac{\text{calls}}{\text{total}} \times 100$ ✓
Mark 2: Substitution: $\% = \frac{288}{426} \times 100 = 0,67605... \times 100$ ✓
Mark 3: Answer: $\% = 67,61\%$ ✓
Total: 3 marks

subQuestions.questionText: Convert 240 minutes into hours and minutes.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Method: $240 \div 60$ ✓
Mark 2: $= 4$ hours exactly (since $60 \times 4 = 240$) ✓
Mark 3: Answer: $240$ minutes $= 4$ hours $0$ minutes ✓
Total: 3 marks

subQuestions.questionText:
INFORMATION 4 — Mr Patel's monthly payslip for May 2026 (TABLE 3):
EARNINGS: Basic salary R28 500,00; Travel allowance R2 500,00; Performance bonus R1 500,00; GROSS SALARY = A
DEDUCTIONS: PAYE Tax R4 200,00; UIF (1% of basic salary) R285,00; Medical aid R1 850,00; Pension fund R1 425,00; TOTAL DEDUCTIONS = B
NET SALARY = C

Calculate the gross salary A.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Method: $A = \text{Basic} + \text{Travel} + \text{Bonus} = 28\,500 + 2\,500 + 1\,500$ ✓
Mark 2: Answer: $A = R32\,500,00$ ✓
Total: 2 marks

subQuestions.questionText: (Refer to TABLE 3 in the question paper.) Calculate the total deductions B.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Method: $B = \text{PAYE} + \text{UIF} + \text{Medical} + \text{Pension} = 4\,200 + 285 + 1\,850 + 1\,425$ ✓
Mark 2: Answer: $B = R7\,760,00$ ✓
Total: 2 marks

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the net salary C.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Method: $C = \text{Gross} - \text{Total deductions} = 32\,500 - 7\,760$ ✓
Mark 2: Answer: $C = R24\,740,00$ ✓
Total: 2 marks

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the PAYE Tax as a percentage of the gross salary. Round to TWO decimal places.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Formula: $\% = \frac{\text{PAYE}}{\text{Gross}} \times 100$ ✓
Mark 2: Substitution: $\% = \frac{4\,200}{32\,500} \times 100 = 0,12923... \times 100$ ✓
Mark 3: Answer: $\% = 12,92\%$ ✓
Total: 3 marks

subQuestions.questionText: UIF is 1% of the basic salary. Show by calculation whether the UIF amount on the payslip is correct.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Method: $\text{UIF} = 1\% \times R28\,500 = 0,01 \times 28\,500$ ✓
Mark 2: Calculation: $= R285,00$ ✓
Mark 3: Conclusion: The amount on the payslip is R285,00. The UIF amount is CORRECT ✓
Total: 3 marks

subQuestions.questionText:
INFORMATION 5: Mr Patel sees a smart TV advertised for R8 999,00 (VAT included).

Calculate the price of the TV BEFORE VAT was added. Round to TWO decimal places.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Formula: $\text{Price before VAT} = \frac{\text{Price (incl)}}{1,15}$ ✓
Mark 2: Substitution: $= \frac{R8\,999,00}{1,15} = 7\,825,217...$ ✓
Mark 3: Answer: $\text{Price before VAT} = R7\,825,22$ ✓
Total: 3 marks

subQuestions.questionText: The shop offers a 10% discount on the advertised price. Calculate the new price (including VAT) after the discount.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Method: $\text{Discounted price} = R8\,999,00 \times (1 - 0,10)$ ✓
Mark 2: Calculation: $= R8\,999,00 \times 0,90$ ✓
Mark 3: Answer: $\text{Discounted price} = R8\,099,10$ ✓
Total: 3 marks

subQuestions.questionText: Determine how much money Mr Patel saved by getting the discount.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Method: $\text{Saving} = R8\,999,00 - R8\,099,10$ ✓
(OR: $10\% \times R8\,999,00 = R899,90$)
Mark 2: Answer: $\text{Saving} = R899,90$ ✓
Total: 2 marks

subQuestions.questionText:
INFORMATION 6 — Simplified annual income tax brackets for the 2026 tax year (TABLE 4):
Bracket 1: R0 – R237 100 → 18% of taxable income
Bracket 2: R237 101 – R370 500 → R42 678 + 26% of amount above R237 100
Bracket 3: R370 501 – R512 800 → R77 362 + 31% of amount above R370 500

Mr Patel's annual taxable income is R385 000.

Show by calculation in which tax bracket Mr Patel falls.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Comparison: $R385\,000$ is between $R370\,501$ and $R512\,800$ ✓
Mark 2: Conclusion: Mr Patel falls in BRACKET 3 ✓
Total: 2 marks

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate Mr Patel's annual tax according to the tax table. Show ALL calculations.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Correct formula from Bracket 3: $\text{Tax} = R77\,362 + 31\% \times (385\,000 - 370\,500)$ ✓
Mark 2: Bracket 3 base: $R77\,362$ correctly used ✓
Mark 3: Subtraction in brackets: $385\,000 - 370\,500 = 14\,500$ ✓
Mark 4: Tax on amount above: $0,31 \times 14\,500 = R4\,495,00$ ✓
Mark 5: Final answer: $\text{Annual tax} = R77\,362 + R4\,495,00 = R81\,857,00$ ✓
Total: 5 marks

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate his MONTHLY tax payment based on your answer to QUESTION 2.3.2. Round to TWO decimal places.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Method: $\text{Monthly tax} = R81\,857,00 \div 12 = 6\,821,4166...$ ✓
Mark 2: Answer: $\text{Monthly tax} = R6\,821,42$ ✓
Total: 2 marks

subQuestions.questionText:
INFORMATION 7 — Investment options. Mr Patel wants to invest R20 000 for 3 years. The bank offers him two options:
Option A: 9% simple interest per year
Option B: 8,5% compound interest per year (compounded annually)

Calculate the value of his investment under Option A after 3 years.
Use the formula: $A = P(1 + i \times n)$
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Substitution into formula: $A = 20\,000 \times (1 + 0,09 \times 3)$ ✓
Mark 2: Simplification: $= 20\,000 \times (1 + 0,27) = 20\,000 \times 1,27$ ✓
Mark 3: Answer: $A = R25\,400,00$ ✓
Total: 3 marks

subQuestions.questionText:
Calculate the value of his investment under Option B after 3 years.
Use the formula: $A = P(1 + i)^n$. Round to TWO decimal places.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Substitution into formula: $A = 20\,000 \times (1 + 0,085)^3$ ✓
Mark 2: Calculation: $= 20\,000 \times (1,085)^3 = 20\,000 \times 1,277289...$ ✓
Mark 3: Answer: $A = R25\,545,78$ ✓
Total: 3 marks

subQuestions.questionText:
INFORMATION 8 — Screen-time survey. Daily screen-time (in hours) of 30 Grade 12 learners, sorted from lowest to highest:
1,5 ; 2,0 ; 2,5 ; 3,0 ; 3,0 ; 3,5 ; 4,0 ; 4,0 ; 4,5 ; 5,0 ; 5,0 ; 5,0 ; 5,5 ; 6,0 ; 6,0 ; 6,0 ; 6,5 ; 6,5 ; 7,0 ; 7,0 ; 7,5 ; 8,0 ; 8,0 ; 8,5 ; 9,0 ; 9,0 ; 9,5 ; 10,0 ; 10,5 ; 11,0

Determine the range of the data.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Method: $\text{Range} = \text{Highest} - \text{Lowest} = 11,0 - 1,5$ ✓
Mark 2: Answer: $\text{Range} = 9,5$ hours ✓
Total: 2 marks

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the mean (average) screen-time. Round to TWO decimal places.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Sum of all values: $\text{Sum} = 184,0$ ✓
Mark 2: Method: $\text{Mean} = \frac{\text{Sum}}{\text{count}} = \frac{184,0}{30} = 6,1333...$ ✓
Mark 3: Answer: $\text{Mean} = 6,13$ hours ✓
Total: 3 marks

subQuestions.questionText: Determine the median of the data.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Method: 30 values → median = average of 15th and 16th values; 15th = 6,0; 16th = 6,0 ✓
Mark 2: Answer: $\text{Median} = \frac{6,0 + 6,0}{2} = 6,0$ hours ✓
Total: 2 marks

subQuestions.questionText: Determine the mode of the data.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Identify frequencies: 5,0 appears 3 times; 6,0 appears 3 times ✓
Mark 2: Answer: $\text{Mode} = 5,0$ hours AND $6,0$ hours (data is bimodal) ✓
Total: 2 marks

subQuestions.questionText: A learner is chosen at random from the survey. Calculate the probability that the learner spends MORE THAN 8 hours per day on a screen. Express your answer as a percentage. Round to TWO decimal places.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Identify favourable values: more than 8 hours: 8,5 ; 9,0 ; 9,0 ; 9,5 ; 10,0 ; 10,5 ; 11,0 → 7 values ✓
Mark 2: Probability: $P = \frac{7}{30} = 0,2333...$ ✓
Mark 3: As percentage: $0,2333 \times 100 = 23,33\%$ ✓
Total: 3 marks

subQuestions.questionText:
(Refer to GRAPH 1: Favourite subjects of 200 Grade 12 learners — bar graph in the question paper. Values: Mathematics = 50; English = 40; Life Sciences = 60; Physical Sciences = 30; History = 20.)

Which subject is the MOST popular?
subQuestions.memoText:
✓ Life Sciences (60 learners) ✓
Max (1)

subQuestions.questionText: (Refer to GRAPH 1 in the question paper.) How many learners chose Mathematics OR English as their favourite subject?
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Method: $\text{Total} = 50 + 40$ ✓
Mark 2: Answer: $90$ learners ✓
Total: 2 marks

subQuestions.questionText: (Refer to GRAPH 1 in the question paper.) Express the number of learners who chose Life Sciences as a percentage of the total. Round to TWO decimal places.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Formula: $\% = \frac{60}{200} \times 100$ ✓
Mark 2: Calculation: $= 30,00$ ✓
Mark 3: Answer: $\% = 30,00\%$ ✓
Total: 3 marks

subQuestions.questionText: (Refer to GRAPH 1 in the question paper.) A learner is chosen at random. Calculate the probability that this learner chose History as a favourite subject. Give your answer as a fraction in simplest form.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Method: $P(\text{History}) = \frac{20}{200}$ ✓
Mark 2: Simplify: divide top and bottom by 20 ✓
Mark 3: Answer: $P(\text{History}) = \frac{1}{10}$ ✓
Total: 3 marks

subQuestions.questionText:
INFORMATION 10 — The Khumalo family has a monthly income of R18 500. The percentages of income spent on different categories (TABLE 5):
Rent 35%; Food 25%; Transport 15%; Savings 10%; Other expenses 15%; TOTAL 100%.

Calculate the amount the family spends on FOOD per month.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Method: $\text{Food} = 25\% \times R18\,500 = 0,25 \times 18\,500$ ✓
Mark 2: Answer: $\text{Food} = R4\,625,00$ ✓
Total: 2 marks

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate how much money the family saves in ONE YEAR.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Monthly savings: $10\% \times R18\,500 = R1\,850,00$ ✓
Mark 2: Method: $\text{Yearly savings} = R1\,850,00 \times 12$ ✓
Mark 3: Answer: $\text{Yearly savings} = R22\,200,00$ ✓
Total: 3 marks

subQuestions.questionText: Mr Khumalo claims: "We spend more on rent than on food and savings combined." Verify, with calculations, whether his statement is CORRECT or INCORRECT.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Identify Rent: $\text{Rent} = 35\%$ ✓
Mark 2: Calculate Food + Savings: $25\% + 10\% = 35\%$ ✓
Mark 3: Comparison: $35\%$ (Rent) $= 35\%$ (Food + Savings) — they are EQUAL, not greater ✓
Mark 4: Conclusion: The statement is INCORRECT. Rent is equal to Food + Savings combined, not more ✓
Total: 4 marks

subQuestions.questionText:
INFORMATION 11 — The Naidoo family has a rectangular swimming pool in their backyard. The pool measures 8 m long and 5 m wide. It is filled to a uniform depth of 1,5 m. They plan to build a paved pathway of width 0,5 m all the way around the outside of the pool. (Refer to DIAGRAM A: Top view of swimming pool with pathway in the question paper.)

Useful formulas: Area of rectangle = length × width; Volume of rectangular prism = length × width × height; 1 m³ = 1 000 L

Calculate the area of the WATER SURFACE of the pool (in m²).
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Substitution: $\text{Area} = \text{length} \times \text{width} = 8 \times 5$ ✓
Mark 2: Answer: $\text{Area} = 40 \text{ m}^2$ ✓
Total: 2 marks

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the volume of water in the pool, in cubic metres (m³).
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Substitution: $\text{Volume} = \text{length} \times \text{width} \times \text{depth} = 8 \times 5 \times 1,5$ ✓
Mark 2: Answer: $\text{Volume} = 60 \text{ m}^3$ ✓
Total: 2 marks

subQuestions.questionText: Convert your answer in QUESTION 4.1.2 to litres (L).
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Method: $60 \text{ m}^3 \times 1\,000 \text{ L/m}^3$ ✓
Mark 2: Answer: $\text{Volume} = 60\,000 \text{ L}$ ✓
Total: 2 marks

subQuestions.questionText:
Calculate the area of the PATHWAY only (the shaded outer ring around the pool). Show ALL calculations.
(Hint: Area of pathway = Area of outer rectangle − Area of pool)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Outer length: $8 + 0,5 + 0,5 = 9$ m ✓
Mark 2: Outer width: $5 + 0,5 + 0,5 = 6$ m ✓
Mark 3: Outer area: $9 \times 6 = 54 \text{ m}^2$ ✓
Mark 4: Method: $\text{Pathway} = \text{Outer area} - \text{Pool area} = 54 - 40$ ✓
Mark 5: Answer: $\text{Pathway area} = 14 \text{ m}^2$ ✓
Total: 5 marks

subQuestions.questionText:
INFORMATION 12 — Municipal water tariff (TABLE 6 — STEP/block tariff):
Block 1 (0–6 kL): FREE
Block 2 (more than 6, up to 15 kL): R13,80 per kL
Block 3 (more than 15, up to 30 kL): R22,50 per kL
Block 4 (more than 30 kL): R35,00 per kL

The Naidoo family used 24 kL of water during the month of May.

Calculate the family's TOTAL water bill for May. Show ALL calculations.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Block 1 (0–6 kL): $6 \times R0,00 = R0,00$ ✓
Mark 2: Block 2 (6–15 kL): $9 \times R13,80 = R124,20$ ✓
Mark 3: Block 3 volume calculated: $24 - 15 = 9$ kL ✓
Mark 4: Block 3 cost: $9 \times R22,50 = R202,50$ ✓
Mark 5: Total: $0 + 124,20 + 202,50 = R326,70$ ✓
Total: 5 marks

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the average cost per kL of water used by the family. Round to TWO decimal places.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Formula: $\text{Average} = \frac{\text{Total bill}}{\text{Total kL}} = \frac{326,70}{24}$ ✓
Mark 2: Calculation: $= 13,6125$ ✓
Mark 3: Answer: $\text{Average} = R13,61$ per kL ✓
Total: 3 marks

subQuestions.questionText: Suggest ONE way the family could reduce their water bill.
subQuestions.memoText:
ANY ONE reasonable suggestion (1 mark):
- Use less water (e.g. shorter showers) ✓
- Fix leaking taps ✓
- Install low-flow showerheads ✓
- Use a bucket instead of a hose ✓
- Collect rainwater for the garden ✓
Max (1)

subQuestions.questionText:
INFORMATION 13 — The Naidoo family is planning a road trip from Durban to Johannesburg. On their map, the scale is 1 : 5 000 000. The straight-line distance between the two cities measured on the map is 11,4 cm.
Note: 1 km = 100 000 cm

Calculate the actual (real) distance between Durban and Johannesburg, in kilometres (km).
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Method: $\text{Real distance} = \text{Map distance} \times \text{scale} = 11,4 \times 5\,000\,000$ cm ✓
Mark 2: $= 57\,000\,000$ cm ✓
Mark 3: Convert to km: $57\,000\,000 \div 100\,000 = 570$ km ✓
Total: 3 marks

subQuestions.questionText: If they travel at an average speed of 100 km/h, calculate how long the trip will take. Give your answer in hours and minutes.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Formula: $\text{Time} = \frac{\text{Distance}}{\text{Speed}}$ ✓
Mark 2: Substitution: $= \frac{570}{100} = 5,7$ hours ✓
Mark 3: Convert decimal to minutes: $0,7 \times 60 = 42$ minutes ✓
Mark 4: Answer: $\text{Travel time} = 5$ hours $42$ minutes ✓
Total: 4 marks

subQuestions.questionText: The family's car uses 8 L of petrol per 100 km. Calculate how many litres of petrol they will use for the trip.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Method: $\text{Petrol} = \frac{570}{100} \times 8$ ✓
Mark 2: Calculation: $= 5,7 \times 8$ ✓
Mark 3: Answer: $\text{Petrol used} = 45,60$ L ✓
Total: 3 marks

subQuestions.questionText:
INFORMATION 14 — Mrs Mthembu plans to visit her son who lives in London, United Kingdom. The exchange rate at the time of her trip is:
£1 = R23,80
(£ = British pound; R = South African rand)

Mrs Mthembu has saved R28 560,00 for her trip. Convert this amount to British pounds (£).
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Formula: $£ = \frac{R}{\text{exchange rate}} = \frac{28\,560}{23,80}$ ✓
Mark 2: Answer: $£1\,200,00$ ✓
Total: 2 marks

subQuestions.questionText: In London, she buys a winter coat for £75,00. Calculate the cost in South African rand (R).
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Formula: $R = £ \times \text{exchange rate} = 75 \times 23,80$ ✓
Mark 2: Answer: $R1\,785,00$ ✓
Total: 2 marks

subQuestions.questionText: Her flight ticket costs R12 500,00. The travel agent offers a 5% early-booking discount. Calculate the discounted price of the flight ticket.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Discount: $5\% \times R12\,500 = 0,05 \times 12\,500 = R625,00$ ✓
Mark 2: Method: $\text{Discounted price} = R12\,500 - R625$ (OR $R12\,500 \times 0,95$) ✓
Mark 3: Answer: $\text{Discounted price} = R11\,875,00$ ✓
Total: 3 marks

subQuestions.questionText:
INFORMATION 15 — Investment comparison. Mrs Mthembu wants to invest R50 000 for 4 years. She compares two banks:
Bank A: 7% simple interest per year
Bank B: 6,5% compound interest per year (compounded annually)
Use: Simple interest: $A = P(1 + i \times n)$; Compound interest: $A = P(1 + i)^n$

Calculate the final amount of her investment under Bank A after 4 years.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Substitution: $A = 50\,000 \times (1 + 0,07 \times 4)$ ✓
Mark 2: Simplification: $= 50\,000 \times (1 + 0,28) = 50\,000 \times 1,28$ ✓
Mark 3: Answer: $A = R64\,000,00$ ✓
Total: 3 marks

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the final amount of her investment under Bank B after 4 years. Round to TWO decimal places.
Determine which bank gives the BETTER investment. Justify your answer using the calculations above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: State Bank A value: $R64\,000,00$ ✓
Mark 2: State Bank B value: $R64\,323,31$; Difference: $R64\,323,31 - R64\,000,00 = R323,31$ ✓
Mark 3: Conclusion: BANK B is the better option because it gives R323,31 more after 4 years ✓
Total: 3 marks

subQuestions.questionText:
INFORMATION 16 — Mrs Mthembu earned R285 000,00 in 2024 and R310 000,00 in 2025. The inflation rate for 2025 was 6,5%.

Calculate the percentage increase in her annual earnings from 2024 to 2025. Round to TWO decimal places.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Formula: $\% \text{ increase} = \frac{\text{New} - \text{Old}}{\text{Old}} \times 100$ ✓
Mark 2: Substitution: $= \frac{310\,000 - 285\,000}{285\,000} \times 100 = \frac{25\,000}{285\,000} \times 100 = 8,7719...$ ✓
Mark 3: Answer: $\% \text{ increase} = 8,77\%$ ✓
Total: 3 marks

subQuestions.questionText: VERIFY, by calculation, whether her salary increase kept up with inflation. Show ALL working AND justify your final answer.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: State salary increase from 5.3.1: $8,77\%$ ✓
Mark 2: State inflation rate: $6,5\%$ ✓
Mark 3: Comparison: $8,77\% > 6,5\%$ ✓
Mark 4: Difference: $8,77\% - 6,5\% = 2,27$ percentage points above inflation ✓
Mark 5: Conclusion: YES, her salary increase (8,77%) DID keep up with inflation (6,5%) and was higher by 2,27 percentage points. Her real income improved ✓
Total: 5 marks
